title: Disk append-log validation
question: Can a restored gem5 full-system run sustain a log-style append workload with periodic flushes and exact replay verification on the current single-core lineage?
feature_claim: Restored gem5 full-system simulation can execute a guest append-log workload that appends ordered records with periodic fsync, reopens and continues appending, then reopens and verifies the full log contents on ext4 while running with FDIP enabled.

why: The guest binary auto-created and targeted a path under /var/tmp rather than tmpfs.
The binary appended ordered records with periodic fsync, closed and reopened midstream in append mode, then fsyncd the parent directory and reread the complete log.
The saved branch trace contains hits on the success-loop branch PC and zero hits on the failure-loop branch PC.
The validating gem5 run used FDIP and the same trusted branch-trace infrastructure already used elsewhere in QPoints validation.
known_limits: This is still single-threaded and single-file, not a concurrent service workload.
The reread happens after flush and reopen, but not after a privileged cache-drop or remount.
This package validates in-simulation disk behavior, not persistence back into the base qcow2 image.
